smart-speaker.definition: An internet-connected speaker that can play audio and respond to voice commands through a digital assistant.
smart-speaker.exampleUsage: The smart speaker set a timer in response to the supported request.

voice-command.definition: A spoken request that directs a device or program to carry out an action.
voice-command.exampleUsage: She used a voice command to request a supported action from the assistant.

wake-word.definition: A word or short phrase that activates a voice-controlled device so it starts listening for a command.
wake-word.exampleUsage: The wake word activates the voice assistant.

routine.definition: A configured group of smart-home actions triggered by supported events, times, or commands.

reminder.definition: A message that helps you remember something.

timer.definition: A feature or device that measures a time interval and signals when it ends.
timer.exampleUsage: The timer signaled the end of the selected interval.

playlist.definition: An ordered selection of audio or video items prepared for playback.

news-briefing.definition: A short summary of important recent news.
news-briefing.exampleUsage: The smart speaker can play a morning news briefing.

intercom.definition: A communication system linking different rooms within a building or ship etc.

multi-room.definition: Designed to work across several rooms, especially for linked audio or smart-home systems.
multi-room.exampleUsage: The multi-room audio system plays the same song in different rooms.

smart-bulb.definition: A light bulb that can be controlled electronically, often through an app, switch, or voice assistant.
smart-bulb.exampleUsage: The smart bulb can be dimmed from the home-control app.

dimmer.definition: A control that adjusts the light output of compatible lighting.

color-changing.definition: Able to change from one color to another, often through an electronic control.
color-changing.exampleUsage: The color-changing light shifted from blue to warm white.

light-strip.definition: A flexible strip containing many small lights, often LEDs, used for decorative or indirect lighting.
light-strip.exampleUsage: A light strip runs beneath the kitchen cabinet.

motion-sensor.definition: A device that detects movement in an area and can trigger another system or action.
motion-sensor.exampleUsage: The motion sensor turns the hallway light on at night.

schedule.definition: A plan specifying when supported smart-home actions should run.

scene.definition: A saved group of device settings used together in a smart-home system.

brightness.definition: The light-output level of a lamp or display, adjustable where supported.

warm-white.definition: A soft white light color with a yellowish tone similar to traditional indoor lighting.
warm-white.exampleUsage: The lamp was set to warm white in the evening.

daylight.definition: In this lighting context, a cooler white light-color setting named for the appearance of daylight.

smart-lock.definition: An electronic door lock that can be controlled or monitored digitally.
smart-lock.exampleUsage: The smart lock records when authorized users unlock the door.

doorbell-camera.definition: A doorbell with a built-in camera that can show or record visitors at an entrance.
doorbell-camera.exampleUsage: The doorbell camera showed a delivery at the front door.

security-camera.definition: A camera used to monitor or record an area for safety and security.
security-camera.exampleUsage: The security camera covers the front entrance.

motion-detector.definition: A sensor or device that detects movement and can trigger an alarm, light, or notification.
motion-detector.exampleUsage: The motion detector sent an alert when movement was detected.

alarm-system.definition: A device or network of devices that identifies dangers such as break-ins, fires, or equipment problems and then issues a sound, light, or remote alert.
alarm-system.exampleUsage: The alarm system sent the warning configured for the detected event.

keypad.definition: A set of buttons used to enter a code or other information into a device.
keypad.exampleUsage: She entered the access code on the keypad.

fingerprint.definition: The distinctive ridge pattern on a finger, which compatible devices can use for identity verification.

app-alert.definition: A notification sent by a mobile or computer application to inform the user about an event or change.
app-alert.exampleUsage: The app alert reported that the front door had opened.

cloud-storage.definition: Online space used to save and access your files from different devices.
cloud-storage.exampleUsage: The service stored the permitted recordings in cloud storage.

night-vision.definition: The capacity to see clearly when light levels are low, such as at night.

smart-thermostat.definition: A thermostat with digital or network features for controlling compatible heating or cooling according to supported settings.
smart-thermostat.exampleUsage: The smart thermostat followed the selected temperature schedule.

temperature-sensor.definition: A device that senses temperature, measures its value, and sends the result as a signal for display or automatic control.
temperature-sensor.exampleUsage: The temperature sensor reported the room’s temperature.

humidity-sensor.definition: A device that measures the amount of water vapor in the air.
humidity-sensor.exampleUsage: The humidity sensor showed that the bathroom air was very humid.

zone.definition: A defined area controlled or monitored separately within a home system.

eco-mode.definition: A setting designed to reduce energy or resource use while a device operates.
eco-mode.exampleUsage: The thermostat switches to eco mode when the house is empty.

geofencing.definition: A technology that creates a virtual boundary around a real location and can trigger actions when a device enters or leaves it.
geofencing.exampleUsage: Geofencing can tell a home system when an authorized phone leaves the area.

vent.definition: A hole for the escape of gas or air.

air-purifier.definition: A device that filters indoor air to remove some particles or pollutants.
air-purifier.exampleUsage: The air purifier runs in the bedroom.

fan.definition: A device for creating a current of air by movement of a surface or surfaces.
fan.exampleUsage: The fan circulated air through the equipment enclosure.

streaming-device.definition: A device that receives media over the internet and plays it on a television or other screen.
streaming-device.exampleUsage: The streaming device connects to the television.

smart-tv.definition: A television with built-in internet features and apps for online content or services.
smart-tv.exampleUsage: The smart TV has several streaming apps.

soundbar.definition: A long narrow loudspeaker unit designed to improve television or home-audio sound.
soundbar.exampleUsage: The soundbar sits below the television.

projector.definition: A device that displays images on a wall or screen.
projector.exampleUsage: The projector displayed the presentation on the wall.

gaming-console.definition: An electronic system designed mainly for playing video games on a screen.
gaming-console.exampleUsage: The gaming console is connected to the living-room television.

universal-remote.definition: A remote control that can operate several different electronic devices.
universal-remote.exampleUsage: One universal remote controls the television and sound system.

hdmi.definition: A standard interface for transmitting digital video and audio between compatible equipment.
hdmi.exampleUsage: The HDMI cable carried the supported audiovisual signal to the display.

bluetooth.definition: A wireless communication technology that allows compatible devices to exchange data by radio.
bluetooth.exampleUsage: The speaker paired with a compatible phone using Bluetooth.

wi-fi.definition: A wireless networking technology linking compatible devices to a local network, which may provide internet access.
wi-fi.exampleUsage: The smart devices connect through the home's Wi-Fi.

casting.definition: Sending or controlling media playback from one device to a compatible receiving screen or speaker.

robot-vacuum.definition: A small autonomous cleaning machine that moves around floors and vacuums dust and debris.
robot-vacuum.exampleUsage: The robot vacuum returned to its charging dock.

smart-plug.definition: An internet-connected electrical plug or adapter that lets a device's power be controlled electronically.
smart-plug.exampleUsage: The smart plug turns the lamp off on a schedule.

smart-oven.definition: An oven with digital or network-connected controls that can provide remote monitoring or automated cooking features.
smart-oven.exampleUsage: The smart oven sends an alert when the timer ends.

dryer.definition: An appliance that removes moisture from washed clothes.

irrigation.definition: Supplying dry land with water by means of ditches etc.

garage-opener.definition: A motorized device that opens and closes a garage door, often controlled by a remote or app.
garage-opener.exampleUsage: The garage opener raised the door when the authorized remote was used.

coffee-maker.definition: An appliance used to prepare coffee.

refrigerator.definition: An appliance that keeps food or other suitable contents cold.

dishwasher.definition: A machine for washing dishes automatically.
